title: Girls Twirl Dress Sewing Pattern – Free PDF

Garment Girls twirl dress with full circle skirt

Level Easy (confident beginner)

Sizes US 2 – 18 (height 91 – 165 cm)

Fabric Cotton poplin, lawn, chambray, cotton-linen, viscose challis

Pieces 5 + a bias strip

This free girls twirl dress sewing pattern is the dress she will want to spin in all day: a neat fitted bodice with a round neckline and short sleeves, sewn to a full circle skirt that flies out as soon as she turns. It goes on over the head with an invisible zipper hidden in the left side seam, so there are no buttons at the back and nothing to scratch.

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Design details of the girls twirl dress

The Girls Twirl Dress is a classic party dress with a simple shape: a fitted bodice, a seam at the natural waist and a skirt cut as a full circle. In our photos it is sewn in a soft butter-yellow cotton and worn with white socks and leather sandals, but it is just as sweet in a small floral lawn, a chambray for everyday or a fine wool blend with tights in winter.

Reading the sketch

The flat sketch shows the seams you will really sew, without the movement of a child spinning. On the front, the bodice is cut in one piece with no darts: the only lines are the curved neckline, the armholes and the waist seam. On the back, the two short lines near the neckline are the shoulder darts (sizes 7 to 18 only; sizes 2 to 6 are drafted on a toddler block with a shorter bodice, a softly V-shaped back neckline and no darts). There is no centre back seam and no zipper at the back: the opening is an invisible zipper in the left side seam, running across the waist seam.

The long thin lines in the skirt are not seams, they are the folds that a full circle makes as it falls. A cotton poplin or a lawn like the one in our photos gives soft, rounded folds; a viscose challis falls closer to the body and swings even more when she twirls.

  • Fitted bodice with a round jewel neckline, finished with a narrow bias facing (no facing pieces to cut)
  • Short set-in sleeves with a softly eased cap and a narrow hem
  • Full circle skirt in two pieces, front and back, for maximum twirl
  • Waist seam at the natural waist (a little higher on sizes 2–6)
  • Invisible zipper in the left side seam, across the waist
  • Back shoulder darts on sizes 7–18

The invisible zipper is the only step that needs a little care, and it is explained slowly in the steps below. Everything else (shoulders, neckline, sleeves, side seams, hem) is simple, so this is a lovely first dress for a confident beginner.

Sizing guide

Choose the size from the child’s chest and waist measurements, not from her age. Between two sizes, choose the larger one: the circle skirt fits at any waist, the bodice is what matters. Not sure how to measure? Read how to take body measurements and how to choose your size.

Kids sizes: US 2 to 18, drafted for a height of 91 to 165 cm. US sizes are a guide only, always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished dress measurements

The finished chest has about 5 cm of ease for comfort and movement; the waist seam sits loose (about 10 cm of ease) so the dress slips on easily. Skirt length is measured at the side seam, from the waist seam to the hem, before hemming. Hem width is the full circumference of the hem: that is what makes the dress twirl.

Fabric amounts

Estimated by laying out all pieces of the largest size in each group, skirt pieces cut whole on a single layer, plus about 8 % for shrinkage. Add extra to match plaids or stripes. Avoid one-way prints: on a circle skirt they run sideways at the side seams.

Zipper and bias strip

A longer invisible zipper is fine: it is shortened from the bottom during the zipper step. The bias strip is cut from your main fabric; the leftover fabric after cutting is plenty.

Common fit adjustments

Length. Each size is drafted for the height in the chart. To lengthen or shorten the bodice, change it at the waist seam (front and back the same amount); to change the skirt, add or remove the same amount all around the hem, keeping the curve.

Growing room. Between two sizes, take the larger one and hem the skirt a little shorter: a circle skirt dress still looks right a season later.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 1.1 to 1.8 m (1 1/4 to 2 yd) of 150 cm wide light to medium woven fabric with a soft drape: cotton poplin or lawn, chambray, cotton-linen, viscose challis, light crepe or a fine wool blend
  • Invisible zipper: 25 cm for sizes 2–6, 30 cm for sizes 7–10, 35 cm for sizes 12–18 (a longer one can be shortened)
  • Bias strip: 4 cm wide, cut from the main fabric
  • Matching all-purpose thread
  • An invisible zipper foot (very helpful)
  • Optional: stay tape for the waist seam

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front bodice: cut 1, single layer
  • 2 Skirt front: cut 1, single layer
  • 3 Back bodice: cut 1, single layer
  • 4 Skirt back: cut 1, single layer
  • 5 Sleeve: cut 2 (one mirrored)
  • Bias strip (no pattern piece): cut 1 on the bias, 4 cm wide

Every piece is drawn whole, with the centre line marked: cut it from a single layer of fabric, right side up, not on the fold. The skirt pieces are large half circles, so assemble them on the floor or a big table.

Choosing fabric for a girls twirl dress

A circle skirt is cut partly on the bias, so it loves fabrics with a soft drape: cotton poplin and lawn, chambray, cotton-linen blends, viscose challis and light crepe all work well. For a winter version, choose a fine wool or viscose blend and add tights. No stretch is needed, the zipper does the work.

Avoid stiff fabrics like denim or canvas, which make the skirt stand out like a bell instead of swinging, and very thick fabrics, which make the waist seam bulky. Pre-wash your fabric the way the dress will be washed, because children’s dresses go in the machine often.

Sewing notes

Fit & style

Fitted bodice, very full skirt. Choose by chest and waist; between sizes, take the larger one.

Fabrics

Light to medium woven fabrics with a soft drape. Avoid stiff fabrics and one-way prints.

Cutting & sewing

Staystitch the necklines and the skirt waist, and let the dress hang 24 hours before hemming.

Printable sewing tutorial

Need help completing the project?

Get the full printable tutorial for the Girls Twirl Dress: detailed step-by-step sewing instructions with clear illustrations, a sizing guide, fabric amounts per size and the list of materials you need.

  • Illustrated diagrams for every step, from the bias-bound neckline to the invisible zipper
  • Size charts, finished measurements, fabric, zipper and bias strip amounts per size
  • Video guides for the key techniques, with links and QR codes
  • Printable PDF with A0 pattern files, instant download
Shop now

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew with right sides together, finish the raw edges with a serger or a zigzag stitch and press every seam as you go. “Left” and “right” always mean as worn.

  1. Darts and staystitching. Staystitch the front and back necklines 8 mm from the edge. Sizes 7–18: sew the back shoulder darts from the shoulder edge to the point, knot the threads and press them toward the centre back.
  2. Shoulders. Sew the front bodice to the back bodice at the shoulders, finish and press open.
  3. Neckline. Fold the 4 cm bias strip in half and press it into a gentle curve. Sew it to the right side of the neckline, trim and clip the seam, understitch, turn it to the inside and topstitch 8 mm from the edge.
  4. Bodice side seams. Sew the right side seam from the underarm to the waist. On the left side, sew only the first 2 cm below the underarm and leave the rest open for the zipper.
  5. Sleeves. Easestitch the cap, sew the underarm seam, hem the sleeve with a narrow 5 mm + 5 mm hem, then set it into the armhole, matching the notches and the shoulder seam.
  6. Skirt side seams. Sew the skirt front to the skirt back at the right side. On the left side, sew from the hem up to the upper ZIP notch only.
  7. Waist seam. Staystitch the skirt waist, slip the skirt into the bodice right sides together, match the side seams, openings, centre lines and notches, and stitch. Press the allowances toward the bodice.
  8. Invisible zipper. Place the zipper along the left opening, mark the waist seam on both tapes, sew each tape close to the teeth with an invisible zipper foot and secure the tape ends to the seam allowances.
  9. Hem and final press. Let the dress hang for 24 hours, level the hem, then sew a narrow 5 mm + 5 mm hem along the curve. Give the whole dress a final press.

Tips and common mistakes

Stretched neckline or waist. Both are curved and partly on the bias: staystitch them right after cutting and never pull the fabric while sewing.

Uneven hem. Always hang the dress for a day before hemming so the bias parts of the circle can drop, then trim the hem level.

Waist seam that does not meet at the zipper. Mark the waist seam on both zipper tapes before you sew, and check it on the second side before you stitch.

Puckered sleeve cap. Pull the easing threads gently and spread the fullness between the two circles; there should be no pleats at the top of the shoulder.

How to style the girls twirl dress

Summer: in cotton lawn or chambray with sandals and a straw hat, like the yellow one in our photos.

Party: in a soft satin or a viscose print with a ribbon belt tied at the waist seam.

Winter: in a fine wool blend with tights, a cardigan and ankle boots.

Looking for more for her wardrobe? Sew our girls puff sleeve dress sewing pattern in the same size range, or the girls circle skirt sewing pattern for a twirly skirt to wear with tees.

Care

Wash as recommended for your fabric, inside out with the zipper closed. Hang to dry so the circle skirt keeps its shape, and press on the wrong side.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) everywhere, including the neckline, and the hems are 1 cm (3/8″), sewn as a narrow 5 mm + 5 mm hem.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download comes in A4 and US Letter, as a printable PDF with one file per size, US 2 to 18.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by the child’s chest and waist measurements. Between two sizes, choose the larger one and adjust the length at the hem.

Is this dress good for beginners?

Yes, for a confident beginner. The only tricky part is the invisible zipper; the paid tutorial has illustrations and video guides for it.

How does the dress open?

There is no back opening: the dress goes on over the head with the invisible zipper in the left side seam open. The zipper runs across the waist seam.

Can I use a stretch fabric?

It is designed for woven fabrics, so no stretch is needed. A very stretchy knit would make the bodice too loose and the zipper wavy.

How much fabric does a circle skirt dress need?

From 1.1 m to 1.8 m of 150 cm wide fabric, depending on the size. With 115 cm wide fabric, count 1.5 m to 2.4 m.

Does the dress need a lining?

No, it is designed without a lining. With a very light or pale fabric, choose a slightly denser weave or let her wear shorts or leggings underneath for playground days.

How long does it take to sew?

About 3 to 4 hours for a confident beginner, plus the 24 hours of hanging before the hem: the dress just waits on a hanger while you do something else.

Can I add pockets?

The pattern has no pockets, to keep the circle smooth at the hips. You can add an in-seam pocket to the right side seam of the skirt, below the waist seam.

Happy sewing!
